conviction_note: abs_move 10.0 (event-implied 10.56 off a 40%-spread chain, median of 7 reactions 10.22, last three prints damped at -1.0/-5.1/+0.55) times a 55 p_up lean from a peer print (High Tide's German volumes) and on-trade proxies for a full summer of BrewDog, offset by heavy post-July dilution; the findings sum to +0.3 and the scaled number is +1.0, both small and the same sign, because nothing here is a company-level number the market has not seen.
bar: FQ1 FY27 revenue ~$265-268m, EPS -$0.18: $264.9m per Earnings Whispers preview 2026-09-30 (https://earningswhispers.com/article/TLRY/20307) and $268.23m in a Yahoo/aggregator snippet (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TLRY?p=TLRY, snippet_only). Two sources within 1.3% of each other; no company revenue guide for the quarter (only FY27 adj. EBITDA $68-75m, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001731348/000117184326004944/exh_991.htm). My bottom-up (Q1 FY26 segments $209.5m: beverage legacy -15%, full BrewDog quarter ~$55m, cannabis +6%, distribution +12%, wellness +15%) gives ~$270-272m, hence +1.5%; inference, not a document.
positioning_check: Short interest 14.38% of float, 5.2 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/TLRY/short-interest/, via sweep). Skew -7.61 vol points (25d put minus call): upside paid. Put/call OI 0.76. Run-up -11.3% over 20 days, -82% from 52w high, 4.6% above 52w low. A crowded-ish short with upside bid: any negative is shrunk for squeeze risk; the positive lean agrees with the skew and is therefore partly priced.

findings.finding: High Tide's Remexian, a German medical-cannabis distributor whose quarter (May-Jul 2026) overlaps two of Tilray's three FQ1 months and which reported on 2026-09-14 after Tilray last spoke, distributed a record 10.2 tonnes, +62% YoY and +35% QoQ, while revenue per gram fell ~10% QoQ (C$38.2m/10.2t vs C$31.6m/7.6t): German demand is accelerating faster than price compression, supporting Tilray's international cannabis line (+34% in FQ4, ~$85m with ~$21m of price compression).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International cannabis growth headlined the 2025-10-09 Q1 FY26 print (+22.09%, international record $22.4m, Germany +134%); the FQ4 print with +34% international moved -0.99% (2026-07-28).
findings.why_not_priced: Tilray's previews (Earnings Whispers 2026-09-30) frame international cannabis as a question of whether 20%+ growth survives price compression and do not cite a peer's German volume; if the market had priced an accelerating German market the stock would not be drifting -11% in 20 days to within 5% of its 52-week low with consensus at only ~26% growth, most of it BrewDog.
findings.independence: Aurora's FQ1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026, released 2026-08-05) put international medical revenue +17% on 'higher sales in Germany driven by increased patient demand' (https://finviz.com/news/377392/aurora-cannabis-announces-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results). Different company, different document. Counterweight already netted in: per-gram price -10% QoQ in the same High Tide numbers, and Tilray's 2026-07-28 call quantified ~$21m of compression.

findings.finding: FQ1 FY27 is the first full summer quarter of BrewDog (UK closed 2026-03-02, $51.1m in FQ4), and it coincided with the World Cup: CGA/NIQ-RSM shows UK pub like-for-like sales +4.2% in July 2026 (strongest month of the year) though only +0.5% in August and bars -5.0%/-2.5%, and BrewDog's own 2026-06-22 release claimed double-digit match-day growth in its UK bars.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beverage drove the FQ4 headline (+61% to $105.6m, BrewDog $51.1m); that print moved -0.99%. No prior BrewDog summer to compare.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus of ~$265-268m implies only ~$270m-level revenue with BrewDog at roughly its FQ4 run rate; a seasonal summer step-up plus the tournament would show up as a consensus sitting above $275m, which it does not. Partly priced: the BrewDog PR is public.
findings.independence: BrewDog/Tilray release 2026-06-22 (https://finviz.com/news/363092/brewdog-bars-draw-record-fan-turnout-as-global-tournament-fever-drives-double-digit-growth) - company PR, not independent of the thesis. Acquisition scale (~$200m annual revenue, $6-8m EBITDA) from https://www.morningadvertiser.co.uk/Article/2026/03/02/tilray-completes-acquisition-of-brewdog. Proxy only: BrewDog has 11 pubs and is mostly packaged/off-trade, and the 'bars' category fell, so sized small; net of the legacy beverage decline filed separately.

findings.finding: Shares outstanding went from 136,203,579 (10-K cover, 2026-07-24) to 147,782,141 (proxy record date 2026-09-24), +11.6m or +8.5% in two months; only ~4.2m came from the 3(a)(9) exchanges of $18m of 5.20% 2027 converts (8-Ks of 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-14, at ~$4.22-4.36), so ~7m shares were likely sold under the $180m ATM opened 2026-04-15, whose stated use is acquisitions while management told the July call it is cautious on US M&A.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline turned on dilution alone; the 2025 sell-offs (-20.7% 2025-04-08, -17.1% 2025-07-28) came with guidance cuts and impairments, not financing.
findings.why_not_priced: The share count sits in a proxy statement and the 10-K cover, not in a press release; the 10-Q will quantify ATM proceeds and a per-share loss on a bigger base. If priced, the stock would already reflect a supply overhang - and partly it does (-11% in 20 days), which is why this is small.
findings.independence: 10-K cover count (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1731348/000143774926024698/tlry20260531_10k.htm), ATM prospectus (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1731348/000114036126014701/ny20066669x1_424b5.htm), exchange 8-Ks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1731348/000114036126036507/ef20081972_8k.htm). Financing question answered: the money buys a debt-free balance sheet and retirement of the June-2027 converts, plus unspecified M&A; no ramp corroborates it, so a mild negative, shrunk for the 14% short interest.

findings.finding: Legacy US beverage keeps shrinking: the Brewers Association put US craft volume -4% in H1 2026, and Tilray stopped brewing at Terrapin (Athens, GA) from 2026-09-25; Tilray's own organic beverage ex-BrewDog was -17% in FQ4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ4 disclosed -17% organic beverage and the stock moved -0.99%; the market has been looking through it.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the decline is a known run rate and analysts model it. Filed because Earnings Whispers names legacy US beer margins (36% from 39%) as a swing factor; a further step down would show in beverage margin.
findings.independence: Tilray FQ4 call summary, organic beverage -17% (https://stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/TLRY/2026/Q4). Industry proxy, small.

findings.finding: Canada's Veterans Affairs cut medical-cannabis reimbursement ~30% from 2026-04-01; Aurora's Canadian medical revenue fell 25% in Apr-Jun, and Tilray guided a ~$4m annual hit to its Canadian medical line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Disclosed on the 2026-07-28 call; that print moved -0.99%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what Tilray already guided (~$4m/yr), so close to 0; filed because the peer number shows the cut biting at full rate.
findings.independence: Tilray call summary on VAC impact (https://stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/TLRY/2026/Q4). Same fact seen from two companies.

outside_window.finding: The federal ban on intoxicating hemp-derived THC (gummies, beverages) was pushed from 2026-11-12 by one month in the continuing resolution funding the government to 2026-12-11; Tilray sells hemp-THC beverages in the US. The decision on a permanent fix or the ban lands after the exit window, though management may comment on the call.

German MedCanG amendment banning telemedicine-only prescriptions and mail-order cannabis passed first Bundestag reading in Dec 2025 but has no second/third reading scheduled; enactment would hit Tilray's fastest-growing line, but nothing is dated inside the window.

baseline_tension: The lean is positive and agrees with the upside-paid skew (-7.6) and a 14% short base, so it is partly priced; it cuts against the -11% 20-day drift, which the dilution finding helps explain.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (narrow proxy loses to a broad series): BrewDog/World Cup finding cut +0.8 -> +0.5, because CGA's broad 'bars' series fell in July and August and BrewDog is mostly packaged beer; the High Tide German finding left at +0.6 as a peer number reported after Tilray last spoke.

Rule 4 + rule 7 (financing is a question; crowded short shrinks a negative): dilution finding -0.5 -> -0.4 after asking what the money buys (convert retirement, unspecified M&A, no ramp) and with 14.4% of float short.

Rule 6 / rule 9 (inside what the market was told; net of the segment): legacy-beverage finding -0.4 -> -0.3, since FQ4 already disclosed -17% organic and it is netted against the BrewDog finding; VAC finding left at -0.1 as inside Tilray's own $4m guide.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): bar sourced to two estimates within 1.3% ($264.9m, $268.23m), one snippet_only, so sizes kept small; abs_move_pct 10.0 and p_up 55 unchanged.
